svg.text: My keyboard, an AJAZZ AK820 Pro, only ships with a Windows configurator, so I
took that apart to get it working on Linux. The HID protocol came out of the
vendor's DeviceDriver.exe: 64 byte feature reports carry the commands, 4096
byte output reports carry the screen as RGB565 frames. With that it runs the
20 lighting effects, per-key colors, uploads an image or a GIF of up to 140
frames to the little 128x128 screen and syncs its clock. There is also a music
mode where the keys react to whatever the PC is playing. A CLI plus a PySide6
GUI with saved profiles, and an installer that sets up the udev rule. Only the
wired USB connection is tested, the dongle and Bluetooth are not supported.
